_judge_provider_note:
ADDED 2026-08-20. judge_provider selects which judge class judge.make_judge builds; judge_model is the id it is given. They are read together and cross-checked (judge.load_judge_model(provider=...)), because ONE judge_model pin serves both providers and a provider flipped without its model would ask Gemini for a claude-* id mid-run.
WHY A SECOND PROVIDER EXISTS: on 2026-08-20 family B moved from Google to Anthropic, which put the judge (claude-sonnet-4-6) and a GRADED frontier model on the same Anthropic account. That account hit its monthly spend cap mid-run and took out the judge and frontier B together, quarantining 147/147 rows of one cell. A new key restored service, but the fragility is structural: a judge sharing an account with a model it grades is one billing event away from ending a run. A google judge also restores the property this project relaxed under duress -- three DISTINCT families, openai and anthropic ablated, google judging.
judge_alternates records the VETTED alternative so the flip is not a guess during an outage.
CALIBRATION, measured live 2026-08-20 against claude-sonnet-4-6 on the SAME rubric bytes.
Synthetic probes -- both providers identical: full-coverage 5, thin 2, gibberish 1.
FLUENCY: no penalty. On a matched pair (same facts, same coverage, one written without the letter 'e' and one in ordinary prose -- compliance confirmed with the shipped banned_letter checker) both providers scored the two texts IDENTICALLY. This was the failure mode that would have disqualified a Google judge: one that docked the stilted prose constraint-holding forces would measure fluency, not task completion, and would systematically fail compliant outputs. It does not.
REAL DATA, 62 rows from runs/g1_r6-char65 re-scored and compared with the Anthropic scores already recorded for those rows (every row Anthropic scored 1, 2 or 3, plus samples of 4s and 5s), 0 judge errors: exact agreement 34%, spec_pass-side agreement 92%. Anthropic 1 -> Google 1 on 8/8, so the degenerate-output floor the judge exists to enforce is intact. The disagreement is one-directional leniency in the middle: all 5 rows Anthropic scored 2 (a FAIL at harness.QUALITY_THRESHOLD=3) were scored >=3 by Google, and ZERO rows moved the strict way.
CONSEQUENCE, stated plainly: the two judges are a FAILOVER, not a substitution. A run must be scored end to end by one of them; swapping mid-run mixes two instruments, and swapping between runs shifts the task-quality floor looser and makes the numbers non-comparable with the committed baselines.
QUOTA, measured 2026-08-20: a full G1 run needs ~1300 judge calls (147 scenarios x 9 cells). 1354 calls were driven through a flash-tier model in one day with ZERO per-day quota errors, so 1300 FITS. The pro tier's generate_requests_per_model_per_day (limit 250) is what killed family B; no per-day metric fired for flash at 1354. The only ceiling observed on flash is generate_requests_per_model = 1000 per MINUTE, which a 2-worker judge cannot approach. Latency is variable (2-53 s/call, ~11 s mean), so the run is wall-clock-bound, not quota-bound. gemini-3.7-flash still returns 503; gemini-3-flash-preview answers but was measured spending 982 thinking tokens and truncating a verdict, which is why gemini-3.6-flash is the recorded alternate.
NOT LIVE. A G1 ablation was in flight when this was added; the configured judge stays anthropic. tests/test_judge_google.py asserts that.
_family_b_substitution: Family B was google:gemini-3.1-pro-preview until 2026-08-20. It hit the Gemini API's DAILY per-model cap (generate_requests_per_model_per_day, limit 250) with an ~11h reset; gemini-pro-latest aliases the same exhausted bucket, gemini-3.7-flash returned 503, and only flash tiers had quota left. A flash model is not frontier, so substituting one would have satisfied R6's letter while making its claim false. Swapped to Anthropic's flagship instead, with Hank's sign-off. CONSEQUENCE, stated plainly: the judge (claude-sonnet-4-6) now shares a family with frontier B. No model scores itself -- they are different models -- but the project's own stricter 'judge is a third family' rule is relaxed. Exposure is bounded: constraint pass/fail is 100% programmatic and the judge scores task-quality only, which drove 2 of 14 failures in the openai cells.
_tuned_history: 'tuned' names the CURRENT published checkpoint; 'tuned_mvp' names the one docs/MVP_REPORT.md documents, and both are commits of the same public repo so either still pulls. They diverged on 2026-08-21 when the v2 checkpoint was published: v2 is the better model (train-split spec_adherence 0.1264 -> 0.1379, median banned-letter occurrences 20 -> 14) and the pin a grader resolves should be the best model, not the first one. MVP_REPORT is left pinned to v1 because it is the record of what was submitted at MVP; rewriting it to describe a checkpoint that did not exist then would make it a different document. scripts/check_mvp.py --pin-key selects which package it is gating, and BOTH must keep passing:   python scripts/check_mvp.py --pin-key tuned_mvp --report docs/MVP_REPORT.md --run-dir runs/mvp   python scripts/check_mvp.py --pin-key tuned     --report docs/FINAL_REPORT.md --run-dir runs/final
